_comment: window_literals: printable strings in a fixed byte window around drift.WINDOW_ANCHOR -- the env block's first field template, not its opening sentence; job is to catch NEW fields cc adds beside the ones this hook reimplements. The two were one anchor through 2.1.235, where the bundler laid the sentence down beside the templates; on 2.1.289 they sit 324 KB apart and a window on the sentence sees no env field at all, so drift.py stands on the templates -- which no longer cluster in the string table either: the pool is ordered by emission, not by source, and on 2.1.289 the window reaches six env strings out of the full set. See drift.py's module docstring; the window is a partial witness, not a complete one. required_literals: each field template this hook reimplements that window_literals cannot see, mapped to its whole-binary occurrence count at pin time — a changed count participates in Task 6's failure, and the exact number's job in that report is to say what moved. Two blind spots land a literal here: under the {12,} length floor (Platform: 10 chars, Shell: 7, and githubCli 9 -- the 2.1.289 field this check therefore missed), or non-ASCII, which forces the whole string to UTF-16 and hides it from the ASCII-only regex (the worktree clause is UTF-16 at 98,150,420 on 2.1.289 and ASCII only in the readable-source copy; the stash caution is the same, and is the one pinned here). Counts are plain byte-substring counts, so they are a lower bound that ignores UTF-16 copies, and most of them are unrelated reuse of a short label — that is fine, because a count is compared against its own pinned value, not against a census. Do not fold required_literals back into window_literals. Derivation of the 2.1.235 baseline, byte offsets and rejected alternatives: notes/env-context-manifest.md — written against 2.1.235 and not re-derived for 2.1.269, so its offsets, its four-anchor count and its `Shell: PowerShell` probe (0 occurrences in 2.1.269: cc moved the `Shell: ` label out of the value and into the field template) describe the older binary only.
